clue.text: Director succeeded in 20s with Coolidge's backing

indicators.note: in says the succeeded letter goes inside the twenties

parts.note: a score is twenty, so twenties are scores
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

indicators.note: the back end of the name Coolidge supplies its final letter only

parts.note: Calvin Coolidge was a US president of the 1920s; only the last letter of his name is used

explanation.surface: A film director made his name in the 1920s with the support of President Calvin Coolidge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside SCORES; Coolidge's last letter, E, goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is a famous American film-maker, so he is an example of a director.

clue.text: Photograph priest on base of Holy Cross

parts.note: a snap is a casual photograph

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, the last letter of the word

parts.note: its final letter is used

explanation.surface: A photograph shows a priest standing at the foot of the Holy Cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy Cross' reads as one name, but 'Cross' is the definition, meaning irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can mean irritable and short-tempered, inclined to snap at people, as an angry person is.

clue.text: Archipelago (or island) welcomes navy

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the island holds the navy inside it

parts.note: a key or cay is a low island, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: A group of islands, or perhaps one island, plays host to the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY with N inside gives KNEY, after OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Orkney is a group of islands off the north coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Einstein's model church features in Spring magazine

indicators.note: the church appears inside the other pieces, as a feature placed within them

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
Time is a US news magazine
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Einstein's theory appears alongside a church in a spring issue of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring magazine' reads like a seasonal issue, but splits into SPA and TIME, with CE between.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacetime is the four-dimensional continuum of relativity, Einstein's framework unifying space and time.

clue.text: Fish covered with some our child sprinkled?

definitions.text: Fish covered with some our child sprinkled?

indicators.note: the fish is covered by the other letters, so it sits inside them
sprinkled suggests letters scattered about in new order

parts.note: the id or ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish dish dusted with something by our child: what was sprinkled on it?
explanation.walkthrough: SOME OUR CHILD rearranged wraps around ID; the whole clue also describes table salt shaken onto fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium chloride is the chemical name for common salt, which is sprinkled over fish.

clue.text: Half of rubbish outside of Ikea is natural fibre

indicators.note: half of means only one of the word's two halves is kept, here its second half

parts.note: riffraff means rubbish or worthless people

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its outer pair of letters, first and last

parts.note: its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: Half the junk round a flat-pack furniture shop turns out to be woven plant fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: Riffraff means worthless people or rubbish; split it in half.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is a fibre from palm leaves, used for weaving baskets and tying plants.

clue.text: Stop sample of nitrobacteria spinning

indicators.note: spinning means turning round, so the letters are read backwards
a sample is a small portion taken from within the word nitrobacteria

explanation.surface: Stop the bacterial sample spinning in the lab centrifuge.
explanation.walkthrough: TROBA sits inside nitrobacteria; turned round it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To abort is to halt or call off a process before it is complete.

clue.text: Outrageous tirade regarding paving stones?

parts.note: a flag or flagstone is a paving stone
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: An outrageous outburst concerning the pavement outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regarding' links the pieces: a flag-rant is a rant about flagstones, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means shockingly obvious or blatant, as in a flagrant breach of the rules.

clue.text: American flower planted in European capital city

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, so the river goes into the capital

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Dee is a British river

explanation.surface: An American flower planted in a European capital city's gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a bloom but means something that flows, here the River Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland, standing on the River Dee.

clue.text: E(0-T) = E(0-T): this cannot be tolerated

wordplay.reading: E + 0 less T = E + 0 less T

parts.note: 0 is called nought; nought less its T leaves NOUGH after E, and the equals sign is read as is

explanation.surface: An equation that looks like physics, followed by an exasperated cry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read each side as E with nought less T, giving E NOUGH; the equals sign is spoken as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom said when someone's patience has run out and no more will be accepted.

clue.text: Clumsy husband leaving bird with dependant

indicators.note: the husband leaving the bird means his letter departs from its name

parts.note: a hawk is a bird of prey
a ward is a person in someone's legal care, a dependant

explanation.surface: A clumsy husband walks out, leaving the pet bird with a dependent child.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop H from HAWK to get AWK, then add WARD; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward and clumsy are synonyms, both describing ungainly or ungraceful movement.

clue.text: Gas mantles oddly missing in recent delivery

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters missing, only the even letters of mantles remain

parts.note: its 2nd, 4th and 6th letters are kept

explanation.surface: Gas lamp mantles have strangely gone missing from a recent shipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping the even letters of mantles gives ATE, after NEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn baby, and a delivery is a birth, so a recent one is a newborn.

clue.text: Audibly quiet object that can be discharged

indicators.note: audibly means as it sounds when spoken, so the word for quiet is heard not seen

parts.note: peace means quiet or calm

explanation.surface: A silent item that can nonetheless be fired off, a little paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: PEACE and PIECE are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Piece is slang for a gun, a firearm that can be discharged or fired.

clue.text: Not spoken with university editor about crank

indicators.note: U and ED go around the crank, surrounding him

parts.note: a nutter is British slang for a crank or eccentric

explanation.surface: Something never said in conversation with a university editor about some eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: A nutter is informal British for a madman or crank.
explanation.definitionFit: Unuttered means never said aloud, which is exactly not having been voiced.

clue.text: Rambling officer in this spot by noon amid rocks

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: rocks is slang for ice cubes in a drink, as in whisky on the rocks
NCO is a non-commissioned officer
here means in this place

explanation.surface: An officer rambles on about being stuck here at midday among the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins NCO, HERE and N, which all go inside ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Incoherence is disjointed, unconnected speech, the quality of talk that wanders without logic.

clue.text: Breeds pigs at main sty regularly to be immune

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

explanation.surface: A farmer breeds pigs in the main sty so that they become disease-free.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on of 'Breeds pigs at main sty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistant means able to withstand something such as a disease, unaffected by it.

clue.text: Scuba worked in sea over more than one summer

indicators.note: in places the worked letters within the other piece
in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards
worked means manipulated, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Scuba gear used in the sea over several summers.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA turned gives AES; SCUBA rearranged gives BACUS, placed inside. A summer is something that sums.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a counting frame used for adding up, so it is something that sums.

clue.text: Unconventional? Not in here from where I'm sitting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: eccentric or radical, as in way-out ideas

definitions.text: Not in here from where I'm sitting
definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally outside, in that place over there from the speaker's view

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the literal sense: not inside, and at a spot away from the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal idiom for weird or very unorthodox, as well as plain location outside.

clue.text: Fever distressing ill boss cured for the most part

indicators.note: distressing suggests the letters being disordered and shaken up
most but not all of the word cured is used, dropping its last letter

explanation.surface: A painful fever afflicts a sick manager who was almost recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: CURE (cured without its D) joins ILL and BOSS, and those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Brucellosis is a bacterial disease caught from animals, also called undulant fever.

clue.text: Desire for the other bikini on vacation in pool

indicators.note: in says the vacated bikini goes inside the pool

parts.note: a lido is a public open-air swimming pool

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outer letters of bikini stay

parts.note: its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: A holiday-maker in a bikini at the pool catches someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: BI goes inside LIDO; 'in' is the containment signal. 'The other' is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual drive, and 'a bit of the other' is a coy British euphemism for sex.

clue.text: Bladder mistakenly grafted with layer of skin

indicators.note: the two words are joined together like a graft, and the answer runs across the join

explanation.surface: A bladder was wrongly given a skin graft by a careless surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' looks like an anagram signal, but the answer runs across the end of Bladder and start of mistakenly.
explanation.definitionFit: The dermis is the thick layer of tissue lying beneath the epidermis of the skin.

clue.text: Animal primarily ate mice and rats aboard new vessel

parts.note: a cat is an animal

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A cat on board a new ship eats the mice and rats.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'ate mice and rats aboard new' spell AMARAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a boat with twin parallel hulls, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Mega-potato in Mumbai raised money

parts.note: M is the symbol for the mega- prefix, a million

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: aloo is the Hindi word for potato, as in Indian menus

explanation.surface: A giant potato grown in Mumbai brought in a lot of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: ALOO read upwards gives OOLA, after M.
explanation.definitionFit: Moola is a slang term for cash or wealth.

clue.text: French runner seconds in front of a German

indicators.note: in front of means the seconds come first in the answer

parts.note: eine is German for a (feminine)

explanation.surface: A French athlete finishes seconds ahead of a German rival.
explanation.walkthrough: A runner is a river here, as rivers run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seine is the river flowing through Paris, and a runner is crossword shorthand for a river.

clue.text: Drug Ceres and Vesta maybe unveiled

indicators.note: unveiled means its covering is taken off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: Ceres and Vesta are examples of asteroids

explanation.surface: A performance drug turns up when the Roman goddesses Ceres and Vesta are unveiled.
explanation.walkthrough: Ceres and Vesta are Roman goddesses, but also big bodies in the asteroid belt; strip off the outer A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A steroid is a type of drug, such as those used to build muscle or reduce inflammation.

clue.text: Element essential for young carbon-deficient bones

indicators.note: the essential part of a word is its core, its middle letter

parts.note: its central letter is used

indicators.note: deficient means lacking, so the carbon is removed

parts.note: the cranium is the set of bones forming the skull
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A mineral that is vital for children whose bones lack carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of young is U; CRANIUM without C gives RANIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is a radioactive metal, a chemical element with atomic number 92.

clue.text: Clocks at watchmakers initially go back-and-forth

parts.note: to clock is slang for to notice, so clocks means sees

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Clocks at a watchmaker's shop tick away, their pendulums swinging back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clocks' looks like a noun for timepieces, but it is a verb meaning spots.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to move up and down or to and fro, alternating repeatedly.

clue.text: Broadcast that's won various things

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so these letters are spread around

explanation.surface: A radio show announcing a prize that has been won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as a programme going out, but it scatters the letters of THAT'S WON.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatnots are miscellaneous items or odds and ends, things not worth naming individually.
